name: Saint John
summary: The last of the three principal islands to enter Danish colonial government.
notes: Informal occupation preceded the formal Danish plantation colony. The 1733 uprising held much of the island and deserves attention even though it did not establish a lasting successor state.

events.title: Spain claims the Virgin Islands
events.detail: The expedition named the island group without establishing a lasting Spanish colony.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Danish colonization formalized
events.detail: Denmark established a plantation colony, expanding from Saint Thomas.

events.title: Enslaved people seize much of Saint John
events.detail: A major uprising challenged the plantation regime before its suppression in 1734.

events.title: British occupation
events.detail: War against Denmark brought British forces to the Danish West Indies.

events.title: Britain occupies the Danish islands again
events.detail: The Napoleonic conflict brought a second occupation.

events.title: The Danish government returns
events.detail: The islands were restored following the European peace settlement.

events.title: Denmark sells the islands to the United States
events.detail: The United States paid $25 million in gold; strategic concerns helped drive the purchase.
